policy.new_capability_rule: Every new kernel capability must map to one existing claim or introduce a new falsifiable claim before it is treated as research-relevant. A feature description alone is not evidence.
policy.review_policy: Reviewers must check that every claim remains falsifiable, evidence status is bounded by observed evidence, proof references resolve, and changes preserve schema compatibility or explicitly version it.

claim:bounded-integration-matrix.falsifier: A selected target or test is omitted/duplicated, compilation repeats inside shard runs, or any successful selective-test step takes 300 seconds or more.
claim:bounded-integration-matrix.statement: PR integration test execution uses one shared build and complete non-overlapping Gatling shards; every selective-test step finishes in under five minutes.

claim:bounded-preflight-latency.falsifier: A stale, missing, malformed, denied, cancelled, failed or mismatched input yields readiness; any applicable source obligation is dropped; bounded resource use is exceeded; or comparable measured collection has no material improvement.
claim:bounded-preflight-latency.statement: The collector removes repeated exact-request reads and overlaps bounded independent metadata retrieval, while preserving all exact-source and terminal custody checks; CI optimizations reduce measured critical-path overhead without skipping applicable execution.

claim:build-layout-compatibility:questio.decision_impact: Determines whether the root lockfile remains an intentional exception to the canonical build configuration directory.
claim:build-layout-compatibility:questio.question: Should a future Bazel release permit the generated module lockfile to move under .config/build, or must it remain root-discovered?

claim:complete-prepush-readiness.falsifier: An empty, stale, skipped-required, mocked-code or missing-provider result authorizes publication, or CLI/RPC/publish bypasses the same boundary
claim:complete-prepush-readiness.statement: Public validate can authorize source PR publication only after all applicable actual source checks and candidate builds pass with genuine current material/provider evidence; release-only packaging is explicitly outside core source scope

claim:created-context.falsifier: A changed, unrelated, dirty, missing-base or tampered event obtains no-change status or readiness evidence
claim:created-context.statement: Only a provider-declared ordinary first push at the verified accepted target is classified as no change; actual candidate ranges remain strict

claim:fresh-provider-metadata-batching.falsifier: An invalid or denied batch falls back to another route, a metadata response is reused across invocations, changed source/provider identity passes, or batching exceeds the existing concurrency/deadline bound.
claim:fresh-provider-metadata-batching.statement: Independent current provider metadata reads use bounded authorized batches; all identity, cancellation, output-bound and final freshness checks remain mandatory.

claim:full-proof-preserved.falsifier: Any missing, failed, stale, mismatched or skipped required proof can produce readiness, or an original check command is omitted
claim:full-proof-preserved.statement: All currently applicable source checks, per-check receipts, exact-source bindings and final freshness remain required under bounded transport and same-checkout grouping

claim:governed-context:question:task-cla.decision_impact: Determines routing policy and whether context selection should optimize for class-specific outcomes.
claim:governed-context:question:task-cla.question: Which task classes benefit most from narrowing, and when is additional context worth its cost?

claim:intent-durability:question:sample-.decision_impact: Determines benchmark power and whether the claim can move beyond instrumented status.
claim:intent-durability:question:sample-.question: How many tasks and agent/tool combinations are needed to separate custody effects from model variance?

claim:measured-latency-reduction.falsifier: Completed comparable successful runs do not show material reduction, or queue and overlapping timings are misrepresented
claim:measured-latency-reduction.statement: The revised collector and grouped runtime lane materially reduce comparable successful preflight costs; no five-minute claim without measurement

claim:multi-agent-custody:question:share.decision_impact: Determines whether shared-interface workflows need an additional claim, protocol, or merge proof.
claim:multi-agent-custody:question:share.question: How does custody scale when tasks intentionally share an interface or require coordinated changes across workspaces?

claim:project-spec-purpose.falsifier: A non-Decapod fixture acquires a Decapod or provider identity, a narrow task replaces product purpose, or supported refresh rewrites authored material.
claim:project-spec-purpose.statement: Generic specs scaffolding and context extraction preserve the configured whole-project purpose across narrow task work; all Decapod specs describe the full product.

claim:proof-backed-completion:question:p.decision_impact: Determines future validation policy and whether additional proof gates are warranted.
claim:proof-backed-completion:question:p.question: Which proof gates best predict production-relevant correctness, and how should warning-heavy but passing runs be classified?

claim:proof-recovery-no-deadlock:questio.decision_impact: Determines whether recovery can be automatic for legacy backlogs or must return tasks to an actionable open state.
claim:proof-recovery-no-deadlock:questio.question: When a task was completed by an agent whose proof record is missing, what minimum repository-native evidence is sufficient for a later agent to recover verification without recreating the original execution context?

claim:regular-release-artifact.falsifier: The staged upload path is a symlink or differs in bytes from the compiled Bazel output.
claim:regular-release-artifact.statement: The release-build uploader consumes an owned regular file containing exactly the successfully built Bazel binary.

claim:release-cpus.falsifier: CPU quota/affinity is exceeded, matrix targets drift, or publication gates are broadened
claim:release-cpus.statement: Release artifact compilation uses runner-effective CPU parallelism without altering global defaults, target matrix or publication gates

claim:release-version-stable-bazel.falsifier: A version-only candidate fails stale-lock setup, or changed dependencies build without a reviewed lock refresh
claim:release-version-stable-bazel.statement: A version-only release with unchanged dependency resolution can build through strict Bazel setup while dependency drift remains fail-closed

claim:validation-without-operator-receip.falsifier: The first checked validation push needs an operator receipt; a changed command/root/head/ref/repository inherits the seal; or unrelated write/provider restrictions are bypassed.
claim:validation-without-operator-receip.statement: Configured validation can create, fast-forward or reuse its exact governed workspace branch without asking the human for a separate local policy receipt; unrelated writes, altered requests and provider/executable denials remain blocked.

accepted-executor-candidate-build.statement: For the supported remote source-CI carrier, plain validation admits candidate helper changes using an independently captured accepted executor, retains the full build/test graph and final controller verdict, and rejects substituted authority or custody.
accepted-executor-candidate-build.falsifier: A changed carrier, altered accepted executor, missing or mismatched dual-root identity, incomplete required graph, or unauthenticated artifact can establish readiness; or candidate helper changes require a separate manual build despite a supported accepted executor.

strict-protocol-rollout.statement: Initial protocol rollout preserves strict independently pinned single-root compatibility, and unsupported workflow or execution contracts remain actionable blockers rather than self-authorizing a candidate controller.
strict-protocol-rollout.falsifier: The fallback accepts altered or new carrier content after only changing the review digest, supported R failure falls back to H, or an old released executable is claimed to acquire unimplemented bootstrap behavior.

checkpoints.summary: Separate accepted execution authority from candidate build inputs, pin the complete carrier in both protocol modes, and preserve controller-owned full validation with versioned custody and regressions.
